<RuleHeader />

Reports a `return;` in the last statement slot of a body that already
completes there: `void f() { g(); return; }` is `void f() { g(); }`.

The return must be owned _directly_ by the method, constructor, or
lambda block — the rule never walks outward through a nested block. A
return nested in an `if`, loop, switch, `try`, `finally`, or inner
declaration keeps its own control-flow meaning (a `return;` in a
`finally` block, for instance, discards a pending exception), and
proving one of those redundant needs a control-flow graph this rule
deliberately does not build.

The removal is target-preserving. JLS §14.17 makes the return's target
the enclosing declaration or lambda, so a trailing `return;` transfers
control exactly where falling off the end of the body does. For a
lambda, JLS §15.27.2 makes a block ending in `return;` and the
fallthrough block alike void-compatible and not value-compatible, so the
edit cannot widen the lambda's target type set.
